title: Constructible common-stage Frobenius and lift data
statement: Fix a finite-field coefficient datum $D,C$ and a common push stage $A$ of the six-functor datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum] [def-sf-operation-stages]. Let $\mathrm{Models}_D$ and its geometric-fiber functor be those of [def-pod-constructible-weil-model-squares]. At each model $X_0$, use the common-stage constructible category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and its derived pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Define $P_X$ to be the recorded geometric-Frobenius pullback [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]; `commonStageCategory` names the inherited category instances and `CommonStage` names this existing push-stage type. The tensor is the recorded common-stage tensor; its Frobenius comparison is the canonical pullback tensor comparison [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison]. The pullback square component is the inverse compositor, the commuting Frobenius-square equality [lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian], and the other compositor [def-pod-weil-lift-interfaces], using the actual geometric fiber map [def-weil-operation-exchange-coefficient-descent]. Define `CommonLifts D C A` as the following data: for every model morphism $f$, isomorphisms $P_X f^*\simeq f^*P_Y$, $P_Y f_*\simeq f_*P_X$, $P_Y f_!\simeq f_!P_X$, $P_X f^!\simeq f^!P_Y$, and $P_X(K\otimes L)\simeq P_XK\otimes P_XL$. The pullback and tensor isomorphisms have precisely the components just defined; the direct isomorphism is the ordinary adjunction mate of inverse pullback exchange, and the exceptional isomorphism is the exceptional adjunction mate of inverse support exchange. Support retains a model compactification and a geometric compactification [def-nagata-compactification]; for separated finite-type $f$, at the geometric base change of the model compactification its carrier is the literal common-stage Frobenius support exchange [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange], and at every other geometric compactification it is conjugated by the stage's comparison isomorphisms. Finally define the pull, direct, support, exceptional and tensor functors on the existing Weil fixed-pair categories by transport through these isomorphisms [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. This defines the normalized data and their functors; no existence or comparison-coherence assertion is included.
